where_it_appears: Press release, LinkedIn job change, system newsroom
detection_method: Job-change tracking on committee contacts + monthly re-enrichment of the CIO seat
why_it_matters: A new CIO re-opens every vendor decision in the first two quarters and is measured on doing something visible. It is the only signal that reliably resets a lost deal.
false_positive_warning: Interim appointments and title inflation. An 'interim CIO' promoted from inside changes nothing; check tenure and whether the predecessor's projects are still funded.

signal: New VP or Chief of Population Health / VBC
detection_method: Job-change tracking + Clay contact search on the VBC and population-health functions
why_it_matters: This hire is how a system announces it is taking on risk. The seat arrives with a mandate and usually with budget, and referral leakage is the first number they are handed.
false_positive_warning: Backfills. A replacement for a departing VP inherits a roadmap rather than writing one - compare against the predecessor's exit date.

signal: EHR migration announced (Cerner or MEDITECH to Epic)
where_it_appears: Board minutes, local business press, Epic community news, RFP portals
detection_method: Claygent on the newsroom and board-minutes pages + tech-stack enrichment diffed month over month
why_it_matters: The migration window is the only period when integration budget is uncontested and every interface is being rebuilt anyway. Arriving after go-live means waiting three years.
false_positive_warning: Evaluation is not selection, and selection is not a signed contract. 'Exploring options' language means no budget yet. Confirm a named go-live date before treating it as Critical.

signal: Epic Community Connect expansion to affiliates
detection_method: Claygent on the newsroom + tech-stack enrichment on affiliated practice domains
why_it_matters: Extends one EHR instance across organizations that do not share an owner, which is exactly the boundary where referral data breaks.
false_positive_warning: Often announced once and rolled out over years. Check how many affiliates actually went live.

signal: New value-based or full-risk contract with a payer
where_it_appears: Joint press release, payer newsroom, investor call transcript
detection_method: Claygent on both sides' newsrooms, cross-checked against the counterparties column
why_it_matters: Downside risk changes what leakage costs from a reporting line to a loss. This is the single clearest 'why now' in the healthcare motion.
false_positive_warning: Renewals dressed as new deals. If the same two parties announced a contract two years ago, this may be a rate change with a press release.

signal: Payer-provider partnership or joint venture announced
where_it_appears: Joint press release, state DOI filings, trade press
detection_method: Claygent on the newsroom + relationship graph across the account universe
why_it_matters: Two accounts in the universe becoming one buying conversation. Also the fastest way to find a warm path into the second one.
false_positive_warning: Letters of intent and pilot announcements collapse frequently. Look for a named entity or a regulatory filing, not an MOU.

signal: Health system acquires a provider group or hospital
where_it_appears: FTC/HSR filings, state AG review, local press, acquirer newsroom
detection_method: Claygent on filings and newsroom + hierarchy re-resolution on the acquired domain
why_it_matters: Creates a funded integration mandate and, usually, a second EHR. It is also the only reliable way to learn that a CRM record's parent changed - HubSpot will never tell you.
false_positive_warning: Announced deals fail state review, and closing can be 12-18 months out. Reparent the CRM record on close, not on announcement.

signal: Payer enters a new state or files new MA counties
where_it_appears: CMS plan filings, state DOI filings, plan newsroom
detection_method: Claygent on CMS and DOI filing pages, re-run before each plan year
why_it_matters: A new county needs an adequate network built from nothing, on a regulatory deadline. Network adequacy is the buying trigger and the date is not negotiable.
false_positive_warning: Filings get withdrawn, and service-area expansions can be paper-thin. Check the filing status, not just its existence.

where_it_appears: CMS public participant lists, ACO newsroom
detection_method: Structured pull from the CMS participant list, diffed each performance year
why_it_matters: Entering or moving up a risk track is a declared change in economics. Exiting is a churn signal you want to see before renewal, not after.
false_positive_warning: Track changes within a model are easy to misread as entries. Compare participant IDs across years rather than names.

where_it_appears: Payer newsroom, conference talks, integration engineer job posts
detection_method: Claygent on the newsroom + job-posting keyword search on FHIR and prior-auth terms
why_it_matters: A compliance deadline with a named owner and an allocated budget. The API work overlaps directly with provider-data accuracy.
false_positive_warning: Nearly every payer will claim a programme. Look for named staffing or a vendor selection before treating it as real.

signal: TEFCA / QHIN participation or HIE expansion
where_it_appears: ONC and QHIN participant directories, system newsroom
detection_method: Structured pull from the participant directory, diffed quarterly
why_it_matters: Shows an organization has decided interoperability is strategic rather than a compliance chore, and that someone owns it.
false_positive_warning: Participation is often nominal. Membership alone says nothing about data actually flowing.

signal: Referral leakage or network integrity programme launched
where_it_appears: Job postings, internal programme names in conference abstracts, RFPs
detection_method: Job-posting keyword search ('referral leakage', 'network integrity', 'keepage') + Claygent on RFP portals
why_it_matters: The prospect has named the problem in public and staffed it. There is nothing left to convince them of except the approach.
false_positive_warning: The phrase appears in stale job descriptions that get reposted for years. Check the posting date and whether the role was filled.

detection_method: Job-posting enrichment with a keyword filter on HL7, FHIR, Redox, interface and integration
why_it_matters: Build-vs-buy is being decided right now. Two or more open integration roles means the in-house option is live and the conversation is time-boxed.
false_positive_warning: Staffing agencies repost the same requisition across boards, inflating the count. Dedupe on the requisition, and ignore anything over 90 days old.

signal: Provider directory accuracy or No Surprises Act exposure
where_it_appears: CMS audit findings, state penalties, class actions, local press
detection_method: Claygent on enforcement and penalty pages, keyed to the payer's legal name
why_it_matters: A published finding converts directory accuracy from a hygiene project into a remediation project with a deadline and an executive sponsor.
false_positive_warning: Industry-wide findings name dozens of plans at once and mean nothing about this one. Confirm the entity, not the sector.

signal: Digital front door / patient access programme
where_it_appears: Newsroom, conference sessions, vendor case studies
detection_method: Claygent on the newsroom + job-posting search on the digital-access function
why_it_matters: Access programmes surface referral and scheduling breakage to executives, which is where the budget conversation starts.
false_positive_warning: Frequently a marketing initiative with no systems budget behind it. Look for a named product owner and an IT co-sponsor.

where_it_appears: LinkedIn job change on a committee contact
detection_method: Job-change monitoring on every contact with role_in_deal = Champion
why_it_matters: A champion leaving is the highest-value negative signal there is, and it is also an opening: they are now a warm contact at a new account.
false_positive_warning: LinkedIn title edits and internal moves read as departures. Confirm the company changed, not just the title.

where_it_appears: HubSpot: email opens and clicks, pricing and docs page visits, form fills
detection_method: HubSpot activity synced into the Audience and scored against the committee, not the company
why_it_matters: The only signal that is already inside the CRM. Its value is as a multiplier: an external signal plus engagement from the right seat is a different priority to either alone.
false_positive_warning: Attributed to whoever happens to be on the record. Engagement from a resident or a recruiter at a 5,000-provider system is noise - weight by role_in_deal.

where_it_appears: HubSpot: last activity date against deal stage
detection_method: Derived in the Audience - engagement 30+ days old with no meeting booked
why_it_matters: Distinguishes 'never interested' from 'interested and dropped'. The second group is the cheapest audience to re-reach and the easiest to mis-file as dead.
false_positive_warning: Deal-stage hygiene is the weak link. A stage that has not moved in 30 days often means nobody updated it, not that the buyer went quiet.
